Chapter 1 · Tips 1–10

Foundations: Users, Requirements, and Simplicity

基础：用户、需求与简单

Get Users Involved As Early As Possible尽早让用户参与进来

Barbee Davis, MA, PHR, PMP · Omaha, Nebraska, U.S.Barbee Davis（MA, PHR, PMP）· 美国内布拉斯加州奥马哈

PAST PATTERNS OF SOFTWARE DEVELOPMENT involved getting user requirements and then going off to do the coding and testing under a veil of great secrecy. After all, the users wouldn't understand what we were doing anyway, right? At the end of the project, our magician's magic cloth was whisked away and the user was expected to "ooh" and "ahh" at the brilliance of what we had produced. However, all too frequently the reaction was, "Well, I know you went to a lot of work, but what I really wanted was…."

过去的软件开发模式是：先拿到用户需求，然后在一层神秘的面纱之下埋头编码和测试。毕竟，用户反正也不懂我们在做什么，对吧？到了项目末尾，魔术师的遮布一把掀开，用户本应对我们产出的辉煌成果发出「哇」「哦」的赞叹。然而，情况常常是：「嗯，我知道你们费了很大力气，但我真正想要的是……」

Today, the secret to project success is to involve the users almost as soon as there is anything visible to show them. How much better it is to find out that there are problems with what we are developing early on, rather than after the project is complete!

如今，项目成功的秘诀是：只要有任何可以展示的东西，就尽快让用户参与进来。能在早期就发现我们正在开发的东西有问题，远比在项目完成之后才发现要好得多！

Costs for changes become increasingly high the further along we are on the project schedule timeline. The time to recode, retest, and rework the immediate software, as well as to test integration with all the peripheral code involved, can delay the project substantially. And both time and cost baselines are jeopardized if a change is so major that it has to go through a lengthy Change Control Board process for approval.

越是在项目进度时间轴上往后走，变更的成本就越高。重新编码、重新测试、返工现有软件，以及测试与所有周边代码的集成，所耗费的时间足以让项目大幅延期。如果变更重大到必须走漫长的变更控制委员会审批流程，进度基线和成本基线都会受到威胁。

Programming decisions over very minor issues, which make perfect sense to the software developer and the project manager, may create chaos back at the workstation when the software goes into use.

那些在开发和项目经理看来完全合理的、关于细枝末节的编程决策，一旦软件投入使用，可能在用户的工位上造成一片混乱。

— p.28 —

I know of a large training company that spent $5 million redesigning its ordering software. Previously, the item numbers matched the product being ordered in a logical way. For example, 4125 might be a student manual, 4225 was the accompanying student exercise disk, 4325 could represent the instructor manual, 4425 was the course outline for marketing purposes, and so on. You could order all the items in the 4X25 series on the same screen.

我知道一家大型培训公司花了 500 万美元重新设计其订购软件。以前，物料编号与所订购产品之间存在逻辑对应关系。例如，4125 可能是学员手册，4225 是配套的学员练习盘，4325 代表讲师手册，4425 是用于营销的课程大纲，依此类推。你可以在同一个屏幕上订购整个 4X25 系列的所有物料。

Each day, administrative coordinators in 140 locations around the world ordered the same kinds of materials over and over and soon memorized the item numbers. Once you knew the number for a student manual, you could immediately key in the numbers for the other items without looking them up, and ordering went quickly.

每天，分布在全球 140 个地点的行政协调员反复订购同样的物料，很快就把编号背了下来。一旦记住了学员手册的编号，你就能立刻敲入其他物料的编号，无需再查，下单非常快。

In the redesign, somehow the project team forgot to consider the way the ordering process was used by the real people doing it. Under the new design, there was no logical relationship between items. Item 6358 might be the same student manual that once was 4125, the accompanying student exercise disk was now 8872, and the instructor manual for the same class was 3392.

在重新设计时，项目团队不知怎么忘了考虑真正使用订购流程的人是怎么用的。新设计下，物料之间没有逻辑关系。6358 可能就是曾经叫 4125 的那本学员手册，配套练习盘现在变成了 8872，同一门课的讲师手册则是 3392。

Not only did the user have to look up each item and try to "forget" the old numbers and system, but also each type of item was now on a separate page. Administrative coordinators were furious. Ordering slowed to a crawl. The project far exceeded its time and cost baselines.

用户不仅要逐个查找物料、努力「忘记」旧编号和旧系统，而且每类物料现在都放在不同的页面上。行政协调员们怒不可遏。下单速度慢得像蜗牛爬。项目远远超出了进度和成本基线。

As a project manager, you should get the users talking to the software developers early and often.

作为项目经理，你应该让用户尽早、经常地与软件开发人员交流。

— p.29 —

Avoid Whack-a-Mole Development别玩「打地鼠」式开发

Venkat Subramaniam · Broomfield, Colorado, U.S.Venkat Subramaniam · 美国科罗拉多州布鲁姆菲尔德

SOFTWARE PROJECT MANAGERS face a lot of pressure to deliver fast. Time is of the essence. How can you get things done fast?

软件项目经理面临着巨大的快速交付压力。时间至关重要。怎样才能把事情快速做完？

Imagine you have two programmers on your team, Bernie and Rob. Both are capable, have the same amount of domain knowledge, and have equal language skills. During development, you find that Bernie finishes his feature implementations much faster than Rob.

设想你团队里有两名程序员，Bernie 和 Rob。两人都很能干，领域知识相当，语言水平也相当。开发过程中，你发现 Bernie 完成功能实现的速度比 Rob 快得多。

While Bernie focuses on getting the code completed quickly, Rob spends time writing code and then refactoring it. He names the variables and methods better. Once he gets things working, he breaks the code into smaller pieces. Now he writes tests to make sure each piece of his code does what he meant it to do. When he's reasonably satisfied, he declares the coding of that functionality done.

Bernie 一门心思求快，赶紧把代码写完；Rob 则花时间写代码、然后重构。他把变量和方法命名得更好。一旦能跑通，他就把代码拆成更小的片段。接着他写测试，确保每一段代码都做了他本意要它做的事。当他基本满意时，才宣布这个功能的编码完成。

But assume you don't know these details. If you only look at the speed with which the functionalities are declared done, clearly Bernie is the better man, right?

但假设你不了解这些细节。如果你只看「宣布完成」的速度，显然 Bernie 更厉害，对吧？

A few weeks go by, and you demonstrate the features to your customer. As usual, the customer loves your completed features, but now wants you to change and improve them. You ask your developers to make those code alterations. When you take the new and improved functionality back to your customer, they try out the features that Rob implemented and are pleased with the changes.

几周过去，你向客户演示功能。像往常一样，客户喜欢你做好的功能，但现在想让你改一改、再优化。你让开发人员去改代码。当你把改进后的功能再拿给客户时，他们试用了 Rob 实现的那些功能，对改动很满意。

* Refactoring: Reworking the body of code to improve its internal structure without changing its external function. It improves the software design. Refactoring code is going back to improve a working feature that was created quickly and tested, now needing further internal refinement to facilitate long-term use and future changes.* 重构：在不改变外部行为的前提下重新打磨代码内部结构，以改善软件设计。重构就是回头去改进一个为了赶工而快速写出、并已测试过的可用功能，进一步优化其内部结构，以便长期使用和将来扩展。

— p.30 —

Unfortunately, they discover something odd with the features that Bernie implemented. While Bernie has programmed in the new functions fine, now a few things that worked before don't work anymore. The customer marks these as defects, and you ask Bernie to fix them. The customer tests the features again. Now even newer, stranger things seem to be broken. What's going on here?

不幸的是，他们在 Bernie 实现的功能上发现了怪事。Bernie 倒是把新功能顺利加进去了，但原来能跑的几样东西现在又不跑了。客户把这些标记为缺陷，你让 Bernie 去修。客户再测，结果又冒出来更新、更古怪的毛病。这到底是怎么回事？

If you have a child, you know what is happening. Bernie has created a Whack-A-Mole application. Whack-A-Mole is a toy. Kids are given a wooden hammer to strike moles that pop up at random. It's fun for them to be surprised by which mole pops up next. However, fixing applications with broken code popping up at random places is not fun. It is frustrating, unpredictable, and it slows your product development. Bernie was sprinting initially, but he was running in the wrong direction.

如果你有孩子，你就知道发生了什么。Bernie 做出了一个「打地鼠」应用。打地鼠是个玩具：小孩拿一把木锤，去敲那些随机冒出来的地鼠。下一只地鼠从哪儿冒出来，孩子们觉得好玩。可是，修一个破代码像地鼠一样随机冒出来的应用，一点也不好玩。它让人沮丧、不可预测，还拖慢产品开发。Bernie 一开始确实在冲刺，但他跑错了方向。

While Rob appeared slower at the outset, he was actually creating superior code. His pace proved sustainable. The better quality of his initial code helped him make workable changes quickly. Plus, the tests he wrote in the beginning gave him instant feedback regarding whether or not his new code was compatible with other parts of the application where the code was used.

Rob 一开始看起来慢，但他实际上写出的是更高质量的代码。他的节奏被证明是可持续的。初始代码质量好，让他能快速做出可行的修改。而且，他一开始写的测试能给他即时反馈，告诉他新代码是否与应用中其他用到这段代码的部分兼容。

When measuring time for a feature implementation, do not consider only the time it takes to write it in the first place. Add the time it takes to enhance, fix, and improve the code. Writing good quality code and tests takes time. It appears to be a short-term loss. However, it comes with a long-term gain.

衡量一个功能的实现时间时，不要只看最初写出来花了多久。还要加上后续增强、修复和改进代码所花的时间。写出高质量代码和测试是要花时间的，看起来像是短期吃亏。然而，它带来的是长期回报。

Ask yourself if you want speed, or if you want to savor sustainable progress.

问问自己：你要的是速度，还是要享受可持续的进步？

— p.31 —

A Word Can Make You Miss Your Deadline一个词就能让你错过交期

Pavel Simsa, PMP · Bellevue, Washington, U.S.Pavel Simsa（PMP）· 美国华盛顿州贝尔维尤

WHICH WORD CAN MAKE YOU MISS YOUR DEADLINE? The answer is "any word." When you are developing a product that will be released in languages other than English, you are adding numerous new risks and constraints to your project.

哪个词能让你错过交期？答案是「任何一个词」。当你要开发一款将以英语以外的语言发布的产品时，你就是在给自己的项目加上无数新的风险和约束。

Some are technical and obvious. For example, if your product will be released in Japanese, it has to support the appropriate fonts. If it doesn't, the Japanese version won't work, even if the English one works perfectly. But font compatibility is not under your control. You and your team need to be aware of translation quirks and consider them before coding. Make sure that the development practices follow international standards that will eliminate such issues.

有些是技术性的、显而易见的。例如，如果产品要出日文版，它就必须支持相应的字体。做不到的话，哪怕英文版完美无缺，日文版也跑不起来。而字体兼容性并不在你掌控之中。你和团队需要在写代码之前就意识到翻译的各种坑并提前考虑。务必让开发实践遵循国际标准，从而消除这类问题。

However, the mere need for alternate language versions also constrains what decisions you can make and when. Typically, localization (Japanese, Swedish, German, etc.) happens in parallel with English development, with a certain lag. It can be a few days, weeks, or even months. However, at some point the translation of the foreign version has to "catch up" with the English version. You need to make sure during testing and reviews that:

然而，仅仅是「需要多语言版本」这件事本身，也会约束你能做什么决策、什么时候做。通常，本地化（日文、瑞典文、德文等）与英文开发并行推进，但会有一定滞后——可能是几天、几周甚至几个月。然而，到了某个点，外文版的翻译必须「追赶上」英文版。在测试和评审期间，你必须确保：

  • What is in the English version can be properly translated.
    英文版里的内容能被正确翻译。
  • What is translated truly corresponds to the English version.
    翻译出来的内容与英文版真正对应。
  • The translated product works flawlessly.
    翻译后的产品运行无瑕疵。

Here's the catch. These three things may be tested after the English version is finished and signed off on. During the testing and reviewing of a localized version, you will always find at least one challenging issue that can't be solved except through a change to the English product.

问题在于：这三件事往往是在英文版完成并签字之后才测试。在测试和评审本地化版本时，你总会发现至少一个棘手问题，而这个问题只有改动英文原版才能解决。

— p.32 —

However, be aware that a relatively simple and low-risk last-minute change in the English product, such as rephrasing a sentence (which takes only a few seconds to code), often requires several days to implement and retest for all the localized versions.

但请注意：英文产品在最后一刻做一个相对简单、低风险的改动——比如改写一句话（改代码只要几秒钟）——往往需要好几天才能在所有本地化版本上实现并重新测试。

This can cost thousands of extra dollars, especially if you are contracting the translation work to an external company. The mistake that less experienced software development project managers often make is simple. They underestimate the effect and magnitude of making unexpected changes to the English version. Here are two main things you can do to prevent this:

这可能多花数千美元，尤其是当你把翻译外包给外部公司时。经验不足的软件开发项目经理常犯的错误很简单：他们低估了对英文版做意外改动所带来的影响和规模。要防止这种情况，可以做两件主要的事：

  • Add a "localization buffer" to the end of your schedule. End of schedule means the effective deadline for any work on the English product included in your project schedule. Any changes that need to be done after that targeted end date must meet very specific and very strict criteria to "get in" to the rework queue. Every change to this version also necessitates changes to the foreign ones.
    在进度末尾加一段「本地化缓冲期」。所谓进度末尾，是指项目进度表中针对英文产品任何工作的有效截止日。在这个目标结束日之后需要做的任何改动，必须满足非常具体、非常严格的标准，才能「挤进」返工队列。因为对英文版的每一处改动，外文版也都必须跟着改。
  • Sequence the tasks in a way that quality control of functionality is done separately from quality review of the English text. That can be as simple as copying all of the English text to a spreadsheet for proofing. That way, unclear wording can be found before the test cycle reveals it on an otherwise functioning product. Now, the necessary change can be done earlier and may not necessitate reworking other language versions.
    把任务排好顺序，让功能质量控制与英文文本的质量评审分开进行。这可以简单到把所有英文文本复制到一个电子表格里做校对。这样，含糊的措辞能在测试周期之前就被发现，而不是等到一个本来运行正常的产品上才暴露。如此一来，必要的修改可以更早完成，也许就不必再返工其他语言版本了。
— p.33 —

Make Project Sponsors Write Their Own Requirements让项目发起人自己写需求

Miyoko Takeya, PMP · Tokyo, JapanMiyoko Takeya（PMP）· 日本东京

PROJECT FAILURE IS NOT JUST A PROBLEM with American corporations. According to a survey conducted several years ago by one of Japan's leading information technology magazines, more than 75% of the projects that are undertaken by Japanese corporations are considered a failure when measured against the metrics of quality, cost, and delivery.

项目失败并非美国企业独有的问题。几年前日本一家主流信息技术杂志做过一项调查，按质量、成本、交付三个指标衡量，日本企业承接的项目中有超过 75% 被认为是失败。

In Japan, as in most other nations, the top reason for failure in each metric is almost always the same: poor requirements definition. The companies that are most at risk are those with poor business analysis capabilities. When specifically reporting on technology projects, such as software development, success is categorized, euphemistically, as "improbable." This result shows how difficult it is to find, identify, and define true requirements for a software project.

在日本，和大多数其他国家一样，每个指标下失败的首要原因几乎都相同：需求定义糟糕。风险最高的，正是那些业务分析能力薄弱的公司。当专门统计软件开发这类技术项目时，成功被委婉地归类为「不太可能」。这个结果说明，要为一个软件项目找到、识别并定义出真正的需求，是多么困难。

Since it is so hard to do, many project owners—such as customers, project sponsors, or company executives—expect the project manager to define and refine the requirements for the software on her own. They do not provide much in the way of guidance or a clear definition of what they need. Since it is a software project, and they may not understand software development themselves, they assume that they don't have to define what they expect.

正因为这件事太难，许多项目 owner——比如客户、项目发起人或公司高管——就指望项目经理自己去定义和细化软件需求。他们不给什么指导，也不清楚说明自己到底要什么。因为这是个软件项目，而他们自己可能并不懂软件开发，于是就以为自己不必说清楚期望是什么。

The software project manager usually does not have the authority or the time to find, select, and prioritize the project requirements on her own—especially since there may be several interest groups involved in the project that probably have conflicting ideas about what they envision the software will do upon completion.

软件项目经理通常既没有权力、也没有时间独自去找出、筛选并排定项目需求的优先级——尤其是当项目涉及多个利益群体，而它们对软件建成后该做什么可能各执一词时。

— p.34 —

It's up to the project manager to spend time with those who are funding the software project to help them define exactly what they want before the project starts. Is it more important that it is done quickly, with few bugs, or on as small a budget as possible? You can't have it all. What resources and skill sets are crucial to create the software they want? Are they making these resources available to the team?

项目经理有责任在项目启动前，花时间和出资方在一起，帮他们把到底想要什么定义清楚。是更重要快速完成、少出 bug，还是预算尽可能小？你不可能样样都要。要做出他们想要的软件，哪些资源和技能组合是关键？他们是否把这些资源提供给了团队？

How will the software be used to run the infrastructure or make money for the company? Are the time constraints realistic? Are they written into a customer contract, tied to an important holiday date, or part of an elaborate marketing plan?

这个软件将如何用来支撑基础设施运转，或为公司赚钱？时间约束现实吗？它们是写进客户合同里的、绑定某个重要节日的，还是某个精心策划的营销计划的一部分？

Without serious, specific consideration of what is to be created on this project during the requirement definition phase, the success of the project is severely jeopardized. Remember, project owners need to convey what they want this software to do, not how the programmers will go about producing that result.

如果在需求定义阶段不认真、具体地考虑这个项目到底要造什么，项目成功就会岌岌可危。请记住：项目 owner 需要传达的是他们希望这个软件做什么，而不是程序员该怎么去做出这个结果。

Convince the project owners that they must be involved in the process from start to finish. Solid requirements planning establishes a clear connection between the business case, project goals, and the project outcome. Otherwise, the project cannot produce the satisfactory result they are expecting. A failed software project hurts the project owners most, since they have put up the money to fund the project and were expecting to use the software to earn back their investment.

说服项目 owner：他们必须自始至终参与这个过程。扎实的需求规划能在商业论证、项目目标和项目成果之间建立清晰的联系。否则，项目产出不了他们期望的满意结果。一个失败的软件项目，受伤最重的是项目 owner——因为他们掏了钱，本指望用这个软件赚回投资。

— p.35 —

Favor the Simple Over the Complex宁简勿繁

Scott Davis · Broomfield, Colorado, U.S.Scott Davis · 美国科罗拉多州布鲁姆菲尔德

AS FAR AS I'M CONCERNED, my microwave oven only has one button: "add a minute." To boil a cup of water for my coffee, I press the button three times. To melt cheese on my crackers, one click. To warm up a flour tortilla, I press "add a minute" and then open the door after 15 seconds.

在我看来，我的微波炉只有一个按钮：「加一分钟」。要煮一杯水冲咖啡，我按三下。要给饼干上的奶酪化一化，按一下。要热一张面粉玉米饼，我按「加一分钟」，15 秒后就开门。

Would a one-button microwave oven ever make it out of the planning committee? Probably not. I can tell by the (never used) features on my microwave that the committee favored complexity over simplicity. Of course, they probably cloaked "complexity" in the euphemism "feature-rich." No one ever starts out with the goal of making a product that is unnecessarily complex. The complexity comes along accidentally.

一个只有一个按钮的微波炉，能通过规划委员会这一关吗？大概不行。我从微波炉上那些（从来没用过的）功能就能看出来，委员会偏好复杂而非简单。当然，他们大概会把「复杂」包装成「功能丰富」这种委婉说法。没有人一开始就想做一个不必要地复杂的产品。复杂是自己悄悄长出来的。

Suppose that I have a slice of cold pizza that I want to warm up. According to the manufacturer's directions, I should press the "menu" button. I am now faced with the options "speedcook" or "reheat." (Um, "reheat," I guess, although I'm kind of hungry. I wonder if speedcook will be any faster than reheat?)

假设我有一片冷披萨想热一热。按照厂家说明，我应该按「菜单」键。于是我面对「快速烹饪」还是「重新加热」的选择。（呃，大概选「重新加热」吧，虽然我有点饿。不知道快速烹饪会不会比重新加热快一点？）

"Beverage," "pasta," "pizza," "plate of food," "sauce," or "soup"? (I choose "pizza," although it does have sauce on it, and it is on a plate.) "Deli/Fresh" or "Frozen"? (Neither, actually—it's leftover delivery pizza. I'll choose "Deli/Fresh," I guess.) "1 slice," "2 slices," "3 slices," or "4 slices"? I have no idea how much longer this interrogation will last, so I press Cancel and then the "add a minute" button.

「饮料」「意面」「披萨」「一盘菜」「酱料」还是「汤」？（我选「披萨」，虽然上面确实有酱，而且它放在盘子里。）「熟食/新鲜」还是「冷冻」？（其实都不是——这是外卖剩下的披萨。那就选「熟食/新鲜」吧。）「1 片」「2 片」「3 片」还是「4 片」？我不知道这场审问还要持续多久，于是我按「取消」，然后按「加一分钟」。

What does this have to do with software development? As far as I'm concerned, Amazon.com only has one button: "one-click purchase." Oh, sure, I had to type in my address and my credit card number the first time I visited, but now I am one click away from my impulse buy.

这跟软件开发有什么关系？在我看来，亚马逊只有一个按钮：「一键下单」。哦，当然，第一次访问时我得输入地址和信用卡号，但现在我离冲动购物只差一次点击。

— p.36 —

Software generally solves complex problems. The question is how much of that inherent complexity are you forcing onto the end-user? Is your software a complexity amplifier? Great software is generally a complexity sink—it bears the brunt of the problem on behalf of the user instead of passing it along.

软件通常是用来解决复杂问题的。问题在于：那固有的复杂，你有多少强加给了最终用户？你的软件是「复杂度放大器」吗？优秀的软件通常是「复杂度洼地」——它替用户扛起问题的重担，而不是把问题往下传。

As a software project manager, are you a complexity sink or a complexity amplifier? The best ones absorb complexity from all sides—from the programmers, from the end-users, from management—and never amplify it. As the end-users generate seemingly contradictory requirements, your job is to help clean them up, rather than passing them blindly on to the developers. As the developers cite arcane technical reasons for not being able to fulfill a requirement, your job is to translate (absorb) that complexity and present the end-users with enough information to help them choose a different path.

作为软件项目经理，你是复杂度洼地，还是复杂度放大器？最优秀的人从四面八方吸收复杂度——来自程序员、来自最终用户、来自管理层——而从不放大它。当最终用户提出看似矛盾的需求时，你的工作是帮他们理清，而不是盲目转给开发。当开发搬出晦涩的技术理由说某需求做不到时，你的工作是把那份复杂度翻译（吸收）掉，然后给最终用户足够的信息，帮他们换一条路。

How easy is it to use your application? How easy is it to add a new feature to your application? How easy is it to request a new feature? Report a bug? Deploy a new version? Roll back a bad version?

你的应用用起来有多容易？给它加一个新功能有多容易？申请一个新功能有多容易？报一个 bug 呢？部署新版本呢？回滚一个出问题的版本呢？

Simplicity doesn't happen accidentally. It needs to be actively cultivated. Complexity is what happens when you aren't paying attention.

简单不会自己发生。它需要主动栽培。而复杂，正是你不留神时发生的事。

— p.37 —

Pay Your Debts偿还你的债

Brian Sletten · Beverly Hills, California, U.S.Brian Sletten · 美国加州比佛利山

DEBT, WHEN WELL MANAGED, is a useful financial instrument for both ordinary citizens and successful organizations. It balances present insufficiencies by borrowing against future surpluses. Used judiciously, short-term debt is an effective tool for smoothing out the rough edges of cash ebbs and flows. When abused, it becomes a burdensome yoke that makes it increasingly stressful to move along.

债，管理得当的话，对普通人和成功的组织都是一种有用的金融工具。它靠借未来的盈余来平衡当下的不足。审慎使用时，短期债务是抚平现金流起伏的利器。可一旦滥用，它就变成一副沉重的枷锁，让你每前进一步都压力山大。

In the world of software development, borrowing time can be a useful strategy for meeting "at risk" milestones, while completing most of what needs to be done. Ward Cunningham introduced the notion of "technical debt" as something developers can incur as they head toward the end of an iteration, or a deadline, if time gets short. At that point, they may not be able to do code right, but by taking some shortcuts they may be able to program code "right enough" to still cross the finish line.

在软件开发的世界里，「借时间」可以是一种有用的策略：在临近「高危」里程碑时，借此完成大部分该做的事。Ward Cunningham 提出了「技术债」这个概念：当一个迭代或一个截止日临近、时间不够时，开发人员可以欠下这种债。那时候，他们也许没法把代码做对，但走一些捷径，就能把代码做到「足够对」，从而冲过终点线。

Even though the software is in a temporary, imperfect state, this is a perfectly reasonable thing to do if the technical debt incurred is managed responsibly. If it is not paid off, however, it will start to become more painful to do over time. Continued borrowing against the future without repayment will put the project further at risk.

尽管软件处于暂时的、不完美的状态，但只要欠下的技术债被负责任地管理着，这样做完全合理。然而，如果不偿还，随着时间推移，还债会越来越痛。持续向未来借而不还，会让项目风险越来越大。

The best way to pay off your technical debt is to assess what "loans" were taken at the end of each iteration. Ask your developers to identify specific hacks they would like to unwind, and quantify how much time they think they need to do so.

偿还技术债的最好办法，是在每个迭代末尾盘点都「借」了哪些「贷款」。让开发人员列出他们想要清理的具体 hack，并估算需要多少时间。

* Iteration: A short period chosen by an agile team (a week, two weeks, a month, etc.) during which a key requirement chosen by the customer is developed, tested, and delivered for approval. The next iteration then begins on the next most important requirement.* 迭代：敏捷团队选定的一小段时间（一周、两周、一个月等），在此期间开发、测试并交付客户选定的一项关键需求供其批准。下一个迭代再开始处理下一项最重要的需求。

† Hack: A quick fix that works but is less than ideal and may need revision when time allows. Fixing inelegant code is called "unwinding a hack." † Hack：一个能跑但不够理想的快速修补，时间允许时可能需要重做。把不优雅的代码改好，叫做「解开一个 hack」。

— p.38 —

They do not need to pay debt off immediately, but it is good to gauge the extent of the needed repair while the shortcuts are still fresh in the developers' minds. Make sure there are specific code problems identified to be rewritten, not just arbitrary buckets of time requested. This is not an opportunity to goof off, it is a disciplined approach to keeping your code base clean.

他们不必立刻还债，但趁那些捷径还在开发人员记忆新鲜时，把所需修复的规模估量清楚，是件好事。要确保列出的是具体要重写的代码问题，而不是随便要一段时间。这不是摸鱼的机会，而是保持代码库整洁的一种有纪律的做法。

Additionally, an increasing array of software analysis tools such as code coverage, coupling analysis, and detection of style deviations can automatically help identify places where debt has been incurred, perhaps without your knowledge. Enter these items into your issue tracking system and schedule them against future iterations. By balancing the workload to include new business functionality and paying off loans, it is possible to keep your technical debt from spiraling out of control while still satisfying customer feature requests.

此外，越来越多的软件分析工具——如代码覆盖率、耦合分析、风格偏离检测——能自动帮你发现那些你可能都没意识到的欠债之处。把这些条目录入问题跟踪系统，安排到未来的迭代里。通过平衡工作量、既做新业务功能又偿还贷款，你可以在满足客户新功能请求的同时，不让技术债失控膨胀。

Software gets unwieldy for many reasons. But it usually comes down to hacks, insufficient documentation, inappropriate dependencies, shortcuts, and deviations from the intended design. When developers throw up their hands and say they need to start over on a system, chances are that unpaid technical debt has become overwhelming. They feel the need to declare the software equivalent of bankruptcy.

软件变得笨重难用有很多原因，但通常归结为：hack、文档不足、不当依赖、走捷径、偏离原定设计。当开发人员摊开双手说要在一个系统上推倒重来时，很可能是未偿还的技术债已经压得人喘不过气。他们觉得有必要宣布软件版的「破产」。

By identifying this debt along the way and dealing with it quickly, you can make more frequent "minimum payments" to prevent ensuing chaos. This metaphor is a surprisingly useful way to explain to business stakeholders how software can become unmanageable over time and why they should invest in keeping code clean.

通过一路上识别这些债并迅速处理，你可以更频繁地「还最低还款额」，防止后续的混乱。这个比喻出奇地好用：它能向业务相关方解释，软件是怎样随时间变得难以管理的，以及为什么他们应该投资保持代码整洁。

— p.39 —

Add Talents, Not Skills, to Your Team为团队招的是潜质，不是技能

Richard Sheridan · Ann Arbor, Michigan, U.S.Richard Sheridan · 美国密歇根州安娜堡

I USED TO HIRE THE WAY EVERYONE IN OUR INDUSTRY HIRED: skills, skills, skills. One day an interview candidate threw cold water in my face, figuratively, and it changed me.

我过去招人，跟我们这行所有人一样：技能、技能、还是技能。有一天，一位面试候选人（打个比方）往我脸上泼了一盆冷水，从此改变了我。

I was looking to add a new hero to my team, someone with years of Microsoft experience. Looking over Bill's resume, I could tell he was perfect for the position. He had over six years of experience in all the relevant skills. If I could hit the right price point, this was going to be easy.

我当时想给团队加一位「猛将」，要有多年微软经验的人。看 Bill 的简历，我就知道他是这个职位的完美人选。所有相关技能他都有六年以上经验。只要薪资谈拢，这事就成了。

Bill came in for the interview. We talked and I described the projects we had on tap, and what a perfect fit Bill was for this position. I was sure this was going well. Suddenly, I realized I wasn't going to get him. I stopped the interview in mid-stream and asked Bill what had happened. I told him he was perfect for the position, but that I sensed he wasn't coming.

Bill 来面试。我们聊了聊，我介绍了手头的项目，说他多么适合这个岗位。我确信一切顺利。突然，我意识到我招不到他。我中途打断面试，问 Bill 是怎么回事。我告诉他，他是这个职位的完美人选，但我感觉他不会来。

His response was, "Rich, if I wanted to do what I've been doing the last six years, I'd stay where I am. I heard you had some cool, new Java projects coming up and I wanted to work here because I saw it as a chance to learn and grow.

他回答说：「Rich，如果我想继续做过去六年一直在做的事，我就留在原地了。我听说你们接下来有一些很酷的新 Java 项目，我想来这儿，因为我把它看作学习和成长的机会。」

That's when it dawned on me. Hiring by running a "resume versus skills" match is the stupidest way a manager could ever build a team.

那一刻我恍然大悟。靠「简历对技能」做匹配来招人，是一个经理能用来组建团队的最蠢办法。

You see, my partners and I got into the high-tech industry because we wanted to be at the leading edge of technology. None of us hoped to spend a career recycling the same skills we learned in college. We got into this game because it would always be about new frontiers and learning new techniques and technologies.

你看，我和合伙人进入高科技行业，是因为我们想站在技术前沿。我们没人希望整个职业生涯都在反复使用大学里学过的那点技能。我们入这行，是因为它永远关乎新边疆、学习新技术和新方法。

— p.40 —

But somewhere along the way, things went horribly wrong. I realized we had stopped investing in our employees' growth. We weren't looking for fresh, new talent. We were looking for very specific, already refined, skills. Now, I tell people that if they see an employer hiring for an exact skill match, what that employer is really saying is, "We don't plan to invest in you."

但不知从哪一步起，事情变得面目全非。我意识到，我们已经停止投资员工的成长。我们不是在找新鲜的人才，而是在找非常具体、已经打磨好的技能。现在我告诉别人：如果你看到一个雇主在招「完全对口的技能」，那个雇主真正在说的是：「我们不打算在你身上投资。」

My advice to anyone seeking to build a strong team is to hire for talents, not for skills. What talents do I look for when hiring technologists for my agile development teams? Good kindergarten skills:

我给任何想组建强大团队的人的建议是：按潜质招人，而不是按技能招人。我为敏捷开发团队招技术人员时，看的是什么潜质？是「幼儿园级的好品行」：

  • Do the candidates get along well with others?
    候选人能和他人好好相处吗？
  • Do they play nice?
    他们能友好合作吗？
  • Do they put their things away when they have finished playing?
    玩完东西会收拾好吗？
  • Are they excited about new things?
    他们对新事物感到兴奋吗？
  • Do they like learning?
    他们喜欢学习吗？

I can teach skills. In fact, in our agile team environment, learning technology is fast and easy. However, it is nearly impossible to teach an adult how to play nice.

技能我可以教。事实上，在我们的敏捷团队环境里，学新技术又快又容易。然而，教一个成年人怎么「好好相处」，几乎不可能。

Hiring for talents, not for skills, is a radically different way to build a team. However, I want to work with those who are poised to move enthusiastically beside me into exciting, new future technology.

按潜质而非技能招人，是一种截然不同的组队方式。然而，我想和那些蓄势待发、热切地与我并肩迈向令人兴奋的未来新技术的人一起工作。

— p.41 —

Keep It Simple, Simon保持简单，西蒙

Krishna Kadali, M. Tech · Kondapur, Hyderabad, IndiaKrishna Kadali（M. Tech）· 印度海得拉巴

STAKEHOLDERS OF THE PROJECT often make things more complicated than they need to be. This is a common cause of software project failures. The team members of the project must have the ability to completely visualize the objectives of the project and complete actual work. Stakeholders, however, can accomplish the project in several simple, magical steps in their own minds. They imagine achieving the end solution quickly and easily, no matter how complex it is.

项目的利益相关者常常把事情搞得比实际需要的更复杂。这是软件项目失败的常见原因。项目团队成员必须能完整地构想项目目标并完成实际工作；而利益相关者呢，在自己脑子里用几个简单神奇的步骤就把项目「做完」了。他们想象着，不管最终解决方案多复杂，都能又快又轻松地实现。

Stakeholders should not build a software project as a monolithic, gigantic, inflexible monster; instead they should allow the information technology team to build it like an onion, with each layer enhancing its maturity. There is no other alternative in the world of reality. Regardless of the completeness of the requirements, there will always be change. If your software is not flexible enough to quickly adapt to changing requirements, the project is dead even before it has begun.

利益相关者不应该把一个软件项目建成一个铁板一块、巨大、僵硬的怪物；而应该让信息技术团队像剥洋葱一样一层一层地建，每一层都提升它的成熟度。在现实世界里，这是唯一的选择。无论需求看起来多完整，变化总会发生。如果你的软件不够灵活、不能快速适应需求变化，项目甚至还没开始就已经死了。

To keep things simple, following are the key points to keep in mind:

为了保持简单，以下是需要牢记的要点：

  • Keep the requirements simple. The business analysts often confuse a particular solution that came to their mind with the actual customer requirement based on a business need. Although the real requirement may be something very simple, there may be a communications gap between business analysts and programmer/developers since neither really understands what the other does.
    保持需求简单。业务分析师常常把自己想到的某个具体解决方案，与基于业务需要的真实客户需求混为一谈。尽管真正的需求可能非常简单，但业务分析师与程序员/开发之间可能存在沟通鸿沟，因为双方都不太理解对方在做什么。
  • Business analysts should write requirements using simple tree-based imagery. The root requirement is the simple objective of the overall project. Small twig sets of child-level requirements are grouped together to form a branch representing a parent-level requirement. This process is repeated on the diagram until each requirement is crystal-clear. Software mind-mapping tools could be used to document the requirements using this approach. Once even a small set of requirements is crystallized, development can begin.
    业务分析师应该用简单的树形意象来写需求。根需求就是整个项目的简单目标。一小簇子级需求组合在一起，形成代表一个父级需求的树枝。这个过程在图上不断重复，直到每个需求都清晰无比。可以用思维导图软件来以这种方式记录需求。哪怕只明确了一小批需求，开发就可以开始了。
  • Follow agile development processes. As soon as a small set of requirements is identified, the development team can start prototyping immediately. Once the prototype is available, stakeholders can test and provide feedback. Customer feedback ensures that requirements are accurate and also helps identify any gaps that developed in the requirements as they were relayed from the actual customer, through the business analysts, to the project team. Allowing the customer to see the prototype also checks that the corresponding solution imagined by the developers is, indeed, what the customer envisioned.
    遵循敏捷开发流程。一小批需求一旦确定，开发团队就可以立刻开始做原型。原型一出来，利益相关者就能测试并给出反馈。客户的反馈既保证需求准确，也有助于发现需求在从真实客户、经业务分析师、传到项目团队的过程中产生的任何偏差。让客户看到原型，还能检验开发人员设想的解决方案是否真的是客户所想象的那样。
— p.42 —

Gaps are translated into new requirements, developers re-prototype, and the cycle continues. Each cycle should be as short as possible—typically, not more than two to three weeks. This cycle of defining a small set of requirements, producing a prototype of the stated requirements, and obtaining feedback ensures that all project stakeholders are always on the same page and everyone is comfortable with what is going on. By religiously following these simple techniques, every software project can reach a successful conclusion. Especially if success is defined as a happy customer and working software that provides the useful business function for which it was created.

偏差被转化为新的需求，开发人员重新做原型，循环继续。每个循环应尽可能短——通常不超过两到三周。这个「定义一小批需求→做出对应原型→获取反馈」的循环，能保证所有项目利益相关者始终同频，每个人都对进展心中有数。虔诚地遵循这些简单技巧，每个软件项目都能走向成功收尾。尤其是当成功被定义为：客户满意，且软件能用、提供了它被造出来所要提供的有用业务功能。

— p.43 —

You Aren't Special你没什么特别的

Jared Richardson · Morrisville, North Carolina, U.S.Jared Richardson · 美国北卡罗来纳州莫里斯维尔

REMEMBER WHAT YOUR MOM TOLD YOU? "You're special! You're unique!" Right, just like every other boy or girl who had a mom! Believing that loving lie leads to common software project problems.

还记得你妈跟你说过的话吗？「你很特别！你独一无二！」是啊，就跟其他每个有妈的男孩女孩一样！相信这个充满爱意的谎言，会导致常见的软件项目问题。

I coach many different teams. Without fail, the teams who believe they're "special" are always behind when judged by how well they meet their software project metrics. Because they think they're special, they have a strong inclination to reinvent everything. They think, "No other team could have possibly developed usable software, or at least not as outstanding as what we create among ourselves." Instead of learning from the mistakes of other developer teams, they insist on making their own mistakes. Over and over and over. At company expense.

我辅导过许多不同的团队。毫无例外，那些自认「特别」的团队，一拿软件项目的指标来衡量，总是落后。因为他们觉得自己特别，就强烈倾向于把一切都重造一遍。他们想：「别的团队哪可能做出能用的软件，至少做不出我们这种水平的。」他们不从其他开发团队的错误中学习，而是坚持要自己把错误犯一遍。一遍又一遍，再一遍。花的是公司的钱。

They spend so much time rewriting, debugging, and putting their own twist on software and tools that are already industry standard that they never finish customer projects. The ones they should sell to people for money. Those mythical, magical products that would be as special as the team, if only it ever got them written.

他们花那么多时间重写、调试，并给那些已经是行业标准的软件和工具加上自己的花样，结果永远做不完该交付给客户、拿来卖钱的项目。那些神话般、魔法般的产品——要是真做出来，本可以和这个团队一样「特别」——却永远停留在想象里。

* Tools: Simple programs that software developers use to create, debug, test, analyze, track, or otherwise support quality software development.* 工具：软件开发人员用来创建、调试、测试、分析、跟踪或以其他方式支持高质量软件开发的简单程序。

To hear this unique group of developers tell it, there are no existing build systems that can handle their "one of a kind" requirements. So, they must write a new one for each new project. Instead of reusing an existing object-database mapping tool, they write their own. Web application framework? We can do that, they profess. Continuous integration? Check. Testing harnesses? Let's write those, too. The vainest and most disillusioned of them will even attempt to write their own programming languages.

听这群「独特」的开发人员说，现有的构建系统没有一个能应付他们「独一无二」的需求。于是他们每个新项目都得新写一个。不复用现成的对象-数据库映射工具，他们要自己写。Web 应用框架？他们说：我们能做。持续集成？没问题。测试框架？也自己写。他们当中最自负、最想当然的，甚至会去自己写编程语言。

— p.44 —

So how do these teams spend their day? Solving the problems they've created by substituting the untested code they built themselves for the fully functional software tools usually available to them for free. When they write their own database layer, they spend the days tracking down obscure performance bugs and caching issues. Handling the edge cases ends up consuming more time than they ever would have spent learning, or even modifying, existing tools.

那这些团队一天是怎么过的？解决他们自己制造出来的问题——因为他们用自己写的、未经测试的代码，替换掉了那些通常免费可得、功能完整的软件工具。当他们自己写数据库层时，就成天追踪晦涩的性能 bug 和缓存问题。处理边缘情况，最终花掉的时间比学习、甚至修改现有工具所花的还要多。

† Edge case: A problem that occurs only at the extremes (fastest/slowest, most/least data, oldest/newest browser). Often means focusing on trivial things that drain time while important work is ignored.† 边缘情况：只在极端条件下出现的问题（最快/最慢、数据最多/最少、最老/最新的浏览器）。常常意味着把精力耗在琐事上，而重要的工作被忽视。

The reason less "special" (but more successful) teams use existing tools is because the problems they're setting out to solve are hard problems. They need reliable tools so their attention is focused on the solution to their software project, not on trying to refill an already brimming toolbox.

那些不那么「特别」（却更成功）的团队之所以使用现成工具，是因为他们要解决的问题本身就够难。他们需要可靠的工具，好把注意力集中在自己软件项目的解决方案上，而不是去重新填满一个早已满满的工具箱。

What does this have to do with effective software project management? Don't let your programmers reinvent the wheel. When they come to you explaining how special their problems are, point out that their mothers may have stretched things when they made that "you're special" assessment. Be knowledgeable about what's available and guide your team toward high-quality open source or commercial tools.

这与高效的软件项目管理有什么关系？别让你的程序员重造轮子。当他们跑来找你，解释自己的问题有多特别时，提醒他们：当年妈妈给出「你很特别」的评价时，可能言过其实了。要了解市面上都有什么，引导你的团队选用高质量的开源或商业工具。

The "not invented here" syndrome derails so many great teams. Don't let it derail yours.

「非我所创」综合征，让那么多优秀的团队脱轨。别让它把你的团队也带翻。

— p.45 —

Scrolling Through Time穿越时间的滚动条

Kim MacCormack · Leesburg, Virginia, U.S.Kim MacCormack · 美国弗吉尼亚州利斯堡

TWELVE YEARS AGO, my team was hired to develop a web application as a subcontractor for a graphic design firm. We were to have no direct contact with the customer. All of the requirements were relayed by the client to our prime contractor, and then passed on to us in a series of random emails.

十二年前，我的团队受雇于一家平面设计公司做分包，开发一个 Web 应用。我们与客户没有任何直接接触。所有需求都由客户传给总包，再通过一系列零散的邮件转发给我们。

One email concerned the screen resolution our artists should use. The previous standard had been 640×480, but more current research suggested that the web site should support up to an 800×600 resolution. (Today the most common screen resolution is 1,024×768.) Even though this was an experienced design firm, its formal requirements (which we never saw) to the customer stated:

其中一封邮件是关于美工应该用什么屏幕分辨率的。过去的标准是 640×480，但更新的调研建议网站应支持到 800×600 分辨率。（今天最常见的屏幕分辨率是 1024×768。）尽管这是家有经验的设计公司，但它给客户的正式需求（我们从未看到）里写的是：

The layout of each page will conform to a fixed 800-pixel width standard and 600-pixel height standard.

If we had seen this requirement, we would have immediately corrected the statement to read, "The layout of each page will conform to a fixed 800-pixel width standard, to support up to an 800×600 monitor resolution." Since we had worked on many websites, we knew that the most important dimension was the width. Users hate scrolling horizontally, while vertical scrolling is considered one of the realities, if not advantages, of using a browser. However, evidently this valuable truth was never conveyed to the customer.

我们要是看到这条需求，会立刻把它改成：「每个页面的布局遵循固定 800 像素宽度标准，以支持最高 800×600 的显示器分辨率。」因为我们做过很多网站，知道最重要的维度是宽度。用户讨厌横向滚动，而纵向滚动被认为是用浏览器的常态（甚至是优点）。然而，这个宝贵的常识显然从没传达给客户。

The content this novice website customer provided for each web page was huge. As a result, very few pages could be completely viewed (lengthwise) on a 15-inch monitor set to an 800×600 resolution. One had to scroll vertically.

这个网站新手客户给每个网页提供的内容量非常大。结果，在一台设为 800×600 分辨率的 15 英寸显示器上，几乎没有哪个页面能（纵向）一屏看全。必须纵向滚动。

— p.46 —

Not realizing we would have to be miracle workers to make this oversized content display on a single screen, the end-user customer got very upset. They blamed our prime contractor, the design shop. In return, the design shop refused to pay us. According to them, we "did not meet the requirements as written.

终端客户没意识到，要让这么大的内容在一屏里显示出来，我们得当「奇迹创造者」才行。客户大发雷霆，迁怒于我们的总包——那家设计公司。结果，设计公司拒绝付钱给我们。按他们的说法，我们「没有满足书面写明的需求」。

From that experience, I have learned the danger of poorly constructed, written requirements and how they can be used against you. It is important to always document your assumptions and insist on reviewing and signing off on requirements with the end-user, not just with a middleman.

从那次经历中，我学到了写得糟糕的书面需求有多么危险，以及它会怎样反过来对付你。永远要把你的假设写下来，并坚持与终端用户（而不只是中间人）一起评审并签字确认需求，这一点至关重要。

Fortunately, agile project management practices have alleviated some of these issues. By recognizing the importance of nose-to-nose interfaces between the developer and the real customer, we have evolved to collectively creating User Stories, and prioritizing features based on the business value they will provide to the customer, rather than requirements lists. A one- or two-week iteration process means we have early and frequent feedback, and the opportunity to clarify customer expectations.

幸运的是，敏捷项目管理实践缓解了其中一些问题。通过认识到开发人员与真实客户面对面交流的重要性，我们进化到共同编写用户故事，并根据功能将为客户提供的业务价值（而不是需求清单）来排优先级。一到两周的迭代周期，意味着我们能获得早期、频繁的反馈，并有机会澄清客户的期望。

Twelve years later, I have run into almost exactly the same situation with a client who is highly concerned about vertical scrolling, even though he wants large amounts of content on the page. Luckily, with the way we run projects today and the lessons I learned from my past experience, we resolved this issue quickly and set realistic customer expectations without the chaos of the past.

十二年之后，我又遇到了几乎一模一样的情形：一位客户极度在意纵向滚动，尽管他想在页面上放大量内容。幸运的是，靠着我们今天做项目的方式，以及我从过去经历中吸取的教训，我们很快解决了这个问题，给客户设了现实的期望，没有重蹈过去的混乱。

— p.47 —
